business_problem: Arcee AI needed to build an open reasoning model for long-running agents that could rival closed frontier systems, but doing so required frontier-scale training, reinforcement-learning post-training, and low-cost inference for a roughly 400B-parameter sparse MoE architecture.
solution_summary: Arcee trained and served the Trinity model family on a frontier NVIDIA stack built for large open-weight models. Trinity Large was trained on 2,048 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs, using HGX B300 systems with NVLink and NVLink Switch fabric plus NVIDIA Quantum InfiniBand to keep expert-parallel MoE training efficient across thousands of GPUs. For data and post-training, Arcee used NVIDIA NeMo Data Designer for pretraining preparation and NVIDIA NeMo RL for reinforcement-learning stages, then combined NVIDIA Dynamo with vLLM, CUDA optimizations, fused MoE kernels, speculative decoding, and KV-cache-aware routing for production inference. This created a repeatable pipeline that spans pretraining, RL, and API serving for Trinity-Large-Thinking, while keeping token costs low enough for long-horizon agents and tool-using workflows where reasoning depth directly affects total cost.

data_flow: Training data is prepared with NeMo Data Designer, large-scale MoE pretraining runs on Blackwell Ultra HGX clusters over InfiniBand, NeMo RL post-trains Trinity models for agentic reasoning, and Dynamo plus vLLM serve the resulting models through Arcee's API and partner distribution channels.
business_outcome: Arcee cut inference pricing to about $0.90 per million output tokens, roughly 20x below leading closed reasoning models, served 3.37 trillion tokens in two months on OpenRouter, and established Trinity-Large-Thinking as a competitive open model for long-horizon agentic workloads.

evidence_quotes: Arcee trained Trinity Large on 2,048 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs, then post-trained Trinity-Large-Thinking with extended chain-of-thought and agentic reinforcement learning (RL) using NVIDIA NeMo open libraries.
NVIDIA Quantum InfiniBand networking was used across the Trinity cluster to keep MoE communication overhead low and maintain training efficiency.
The training pipeline incorporated NVIDIA NeMo™ Data Designer for pretraining data preparation and NVIDIA NeMo RL for RL post-training.
Arcee combined NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra with NVIDIA Dynamo and vLLM for optimized inference.
Inference via Arcee's API costs around $0.90 per 1M output tokens, around 20x cheaper than leading closed reasoning models.
